## 1. Public API Consistency

`RegistryClient::is_published` (callisto-model/src/registry.rs:42) and the tag-resolution pair in callisto-graph/src/tags.rs illustrate genuine "looks-alike, behaves-differently" traps:

- `last_tag_for` (tags.rs:85) returns `Result<LastTagSelection, GraphError>` — errors on failure — while `TagIndex::last_tag` (tags.rs:135) returns `Option<&LastTag>` for the *same conceptual lookup*, silently swallowing "no tag found" into `None` with no error path. A contributor extending tag resolution has to read both implementations to know which failure mode applies where; the doc comment at tags.rs:77-84 partially compensates but only for `last_tag_for`.
- Error typing is inconsistent even within one crate: `callisto-model/src/registry.rs` has a proper `thiserror` enum `RegistryError` (RateLimited/AuthFailed/Network/Other), but `Other(String)` is used as an escape hatch in `publish_client.rs` for genuinely distinct failure classes — e.g. line 97 (`Err(RegistryError::Other(format!("npm view failed ambiguously...")))`), line 155 (`unsupported package identity`), and line 180 (`no subprocess publisher configured`). These are three semantically different situations (ambiguous CLI output, unimplemented ecosystem, config gap) all collapsed into the same catch-all variant a caller can't `match` on distinctly, unlike `CommandError`/`ManifestError`/`VcsError` which use precise, matchable variants throughout.

## 2. Doc Comment Coverage/Quality

This session's additions (tags.rs, publish_client.rs) set a noticeably *higher* bar than older code: tags.rs:13-32, 44-51, 66-67, 77-84 each explain *why* (wasm32 constraints, batching rationale, byte-identical-selection guarantees) with cross-references via `[...]` intradoc links; publish_client.rs:1-24 has a full module-level doc explaining the deliberate design constraint (no direct registry HTTP calls) and an explicit "Known trait-boundary limitation" section admitting the `PublishPlan` metadata isn't threaded through.

By contrast, `crates/callisto-model/src/registry.rs`'s `RateLimitPolicy`/`TimeProvider` traits (lines 53-60) have zero doc comments despite being just as load-bearing, and `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs`'s `solve_cascade` (line 160) — arguably the most complex function in the crate — has no top-level doc comment explaining invariants/panics, only inline comments scattered through the body. `crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs`'s `CommandRunner` trait (line 6) is one line: "Trait for executing subprocess commands," with no mention of the cwd contract or blocking semantics. The inconsistency isn't just old-vs-new; it's that this session raised the doc bar for touched files without back-filling adjacent, equally-central pre-existing APIs, so a contributor's expectation of doc depth will vary wildly depending which file they open next.

## 3. Test-Double Duplication

At least 9 independent, hand-rolled `CommandRunner` test doubles exist with no shared module:
- `FakeGitTagRunner` (tags.rs:198) — counts calls, returns canned `git tag --list` output
- `ScriptedRunner` (publish_client.rs:319) — returns one fixed `CommandOutput`
- `NoopRunner` (graph/tests/manifest_cache_test.rs:22), `RealGitRunner`/`PoisonedRunner` (aggregate.rs:414/453), `DryRunTestRunner`/`ValidateArgTestRunner`/`DummyRunner`×2 (graph_tests.rs:417/476/532/572), `PoisonedRunner` (conventional/window.rs:66)

This is real duplication a shared test-utilities crate could consolidate — none of the existing scoping choices look deliberate (e.g. crate-boundary-driven); they read as independently reinvented each time a new test needed a fake runner.

## 4. Error Message Actionability

`GraphError`, `VcsError`, and `ManifestError` are generally strong: `ManifestError::DependencyNotFound` (callisto-model/src/error.rs:129-135) includes `path`, `name`, and `kind`; `GraphError::DuplicatePackage` (error.rs:56-61) lists every conflicting path; `VcsError`'s discovery variant (vcs/lib.rs:8-9) includes both `path` and the underlying `message`. The one weak spot is the `RegistryError::Other`/`GraphError::Command`-via-`RegistryError::Other` path noted in §1: `SubprocessRegistryClient::run` (publish_client.rs:52-56) maps *every* `CommandError` into `RegistryError::Other(e.to_string())`, discarding the original `CommandError` variant (`NotFound` vs `Failed` vs `Io` have very different debugging implications) and losing the structured `program`/`exit_code`/`stderr` fields in favor of a flattened string — the opposite of `GraphError::Command`'s `#[from] CommandError` (error.rs:53-54), which preserves the full structured error via `thiserror`'s `#[error(transparent)]`-adjacent forwarding.</result>

## New bug found (not just missing coverage)

### [Medium] `apply_version_plan` silently discards git staging failures, then reports success anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:182` and `:191` (`drop(runner.run("git", &args, root));`)
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback (Taxonomy 4)
- **Root Cause**: `CommandRunner::run` returns `Result<CommandOutput, CommandError>`, and `CommandOutput` can itself report non-zero `exit_code` without being an `Err`. Both call sites (`git add --`, `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch --`) pipe the result straight into `drop(...)`, discarding process-spawn errors and non-zero exits alike. Immediately after, `outcome.staged = modified_paths;` is set unconditionally — the caller has no way to know staging actually failed.
- **Failing Scenario**: workspace root is not a git repo (or `git` binary missing, or a permission/lock error) during `callisto version`/`apply`; manifests/changelog are written to disk correctly, but `outcome.staged` still reports every path as staged. A caller that trusts `staged` to decide whether to run `git commit` would commit nothing (or commit only some files) while believing the full set succeeded.
- **Verification Strategy**: mock `CommandRunner` to return `Ok(CommandOutput{exit_code: Some(1), ..})` (or `Err`) for the `git add` call; assert `apply_version_plan` either propagates an error or omits/flags the affected paths in `ApplyOutcome`, rather than silently reporting them as staged.

## Coverage gaps by area

**1. `resolver.rs` / `walk.rs` / `plan.rs` / `apply.rs`**
`ManifestWalkResolver::build` (walk.rs) and `apply_version_plan` (apply.rs) have zero dedicated unit tests in these files, and no `tests/*.rs` file exercises `ManifestWalkResolver::build` directly (only indirectly via `graph_tests.rs`'s higher-level fixtures, which are happy-path workspace layouts). Missing: empty workspace (no projects found), a package present in multiple ecosystems at the same path (the `by_path`/`list.sort_by_key`/`primary_id = list[0]` logic — untested tie-break when e.g. both Cargo and npm manifests exist at one path), a dependency that can't be resolved (`index.resolve_native` returns `None` — silently dropped, no diagnostic, untested), and manifest-open failure (`if let Ok(m) = open_cached(...)` swallows errors with no diagnostic — untested). `apply_version_plan` has no test for: a bump whose manifest write fails partway through a multi-target `bump.writes` list (partial-write crash safety), `consumed_changesets` path that doesn't exist (silently skipped, no error — untested), or `pre_state_update`/`delete_pre_json` mutual-exclusion edge cases.

`toposort_impl` (toposort.rs) has only 2 tests (linear, self-loop cycle). Missing: multi-node (3+) cycle extraction, a subset id absent from `all_packages` (the `UnknownPackage` error path is entirely untested), and — most importantly — no test asserts that `Dev`/`Peer` `DepKind` edges are excluded from ordering constraints (`toposort.rs:31-33`'s `matches!` filter). A future edit widening that filter to include `Dev` would silently create false ordering dependencies with no test catching it.

**2. `locate/` (workspace discovery)**
`ignore_walk.rs` (`IgnoreWalkLocator::projects`, `to_workspace_relative`) and `root.rs` (`find_workspace_root`, `is_workspace_root`) have **no tests at all**, inline or in `tests/`. This is a complete blind spot, not just happy-path bias, for: symlinked project directories, nested Cargo/npm workspaces (inner workspace root should probably stop discovery but there's no test proving it does or doesn't), `.gitignore`-excluded package directories, malformed/unparseable `Cargo.toml`/`package.json`/`pyproject.toml` (silently skipped via `if let Ok(...)` — no diagnostic), a `Cargo.toml` with `[package]` but unparseable TOML, and `find_workspace_root` walking to filesystem root with no workspace marker (only the `Err` path exists, untested).

**3. `callisto-conventional`**
`commit.rs` has 3 tests (feat+breaking, body-with-colon, UTF-8 BOM) — good but narrow. Missing: multiple `BREAKING CHANGE`/`BREAKING-CHANGE` footers in one commit (does severity/breaking flag behave correctly, are both footers retained separately), malformed scope (`feat(: desc`, `feat(a(b)): desc` nested parens, `feat(): desc` empty scope), empty/whitespace-only commit message (only reachable via the early-return paths, never asserted), non-ASCII/emoji descriptions and scopes, and a footer block colliding with a hyphenated-token body line (`is_valid_footer_token` accepts anything `Word-word`, e.g. a body line like `Co-authored: someone` could be misclassified as a footer if it's in the trailing block — untested boundary). `severity.rs` covers all 4 branches reasonably. `pre_cursor.rs` (`resolve_pre_cursor`, `advance_pre_cursor`) has **zero tests anywhere** — missing coverage for `git rev-parse` returning non-zero/empty stdout (`Ok(None)` path), a ref pointing at a malformed/non-SHA value (`MalformedPreCursorRef`), and `advance_pre_cursor`'s failure path (`PreCursorAdvanceFailed`).

**4. `callisto-changelog` beyond `write.rs`**
`render.rs` has exactly one test covering only a single `ChangeSource::Changeset` entry with `to: Some(...)`. Untested: `ChangeSource::Commit`, `DependencyUpdate` (the `dep_updates` batching block), `PeerEscalation`, `GroupUnion`, `NewGroupMember` variants; `to: None` → `## Unreleased` heading; empty `entries` → `EmptyInput` error; mixed severities across all three sections in one call (ordering/spacing between sections). `group.rs`'s `group_entries` has **zero tests** — the `Severity::None → SeverityNoneEntry` error path and multi-severity partitioning are completely unverified.

**5. `snapshot.rs` / `tag.rs` / `init.rs`**
Beyond the already-logged confirmed bugs: `test_snapshot_version_template_placeholders` and `test_tag_dry_run_does_not_create_git_tags` (`crates/callisto-graph/tests/graph_tests.rs:393,529`) are single-package, single-tag happy paths only — no test for zero packages, a pre-existing tag (idempotent `already_existed` reporting), or a failing `git tag -a` subprocess. `init.rs` has **no test coverage anywhere in the repo** (confirmed via repo-wide grep) — not even for the documented happy path (first-run file creation, `InitReport.initialized` flag correctness, idempotent re-run when `callisto.toml`/`.changeset/` already exist).</result>

Should we git rid of the gix usage and make it all wasm compatible? Or do we duplicate some of this work with two paths to support moon?

No — don't try to eliminate gix and make everything wasm-compatible. Two reasons, and they both point the same direction:

**It's not currently possible.** The spike proved this concretely: `gix-odb`/`gix-pack`/`gix-index` all hit `memmap2`'s hard WASI wall for actual object-content reads. The only way around it is forking three upstream crates and maintaining that fork indefinitely, for a benefit that turns out not to exist (see next point).

**Even if it were possible, you wouldn't want it.** This is the more important answer. The industry research this session did wasn't just "is gix WASM-viable" — it checked whether host-mediated access is the *correct* architecture for WASM guests generally, independent of gix. It is: Extism has a stated, explicit policy against direct in-guest filesystem access for security reasons; proxy-wasm/Envoy, OPA's WASM target, and Cloudflare Workers all converge on the identical pattern — native/OS capabilities stay host-side, guest gets a marshaled bridge, no exceptions. So a working in-guest gix wouldn't be "the real fix we were forced to work around" — it'd be the architecturally wrong choice you'd have talked yourself into because it happened to become possible.

So yes, two paths — but frame it as two backends behind one abstraction, not duplicated work. And the amount of actual duplication is small if you do it right: the *logic* that decides things (which tag wins, glob matching, version selection) already lives in one place as pure functions (`select_last_tag`, `matching_tags`) that both backends feed into — that's exactly what the `tags.rs` fix already established. The only thing that differs per backend is the raw "get bytes from git" step: `gix` calls natively, `git <subcommand>` via `CommandRunner` on wasm. That's a thin seam, not a fork of the whole git-access layer.

Which is exactly why the earlier recommendation stands: formalize it as a real trait (something like `GitDataSource` in `callisto-vcs`, with `NativeGix`/`CommandRunnerFallback` implementations) instead of the current hand-rolled "try gix, fall through" duplicated per call site — that's what turns "two paths" from a maintenance liability into a clean, intentional architecture. That's exactly the gap the sweep just found three more instances of (`tag.rs`, `window.rs`, `aggregate.rs`'s own `resolve_since`). Worth adding to the next planning pass once the current fix batches land.

## Report

**Bug**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:182,191` used `drop(runner.run(...))`, discarding both spawn errors and non-zero git exit codes, then unconditionally set `outcome.staged = modified_paths` regardless of whether `git add`/`git rm --cached` actually succeeded.

**Design decision: fatal error (propagate via `Result<ApplyOutcome, GraphError>`), not accurately-reported partial success.**

Reasoning:
- I grepped for all consumers of `ApplyOutcome.staged` (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs`, `snapshot.rs`) — neither actually reads `.staged` today (only `.lockfile_refresh_results` is used from the outcome). There's no existing branch logic that would benefit from a nuanced "staged: false" signal; nothing downstream conditionally runs `git commit` based on this field.
- `GraphError` already has a `Command(#[from] callisto_model::CommandError)` variant, and `CommandError::Failed { program, exit_code, stderr }` exists specifically for this purpose but was unused by any git-command call site in `apply.rs`.
- The existing precedent in this same crate (`commands/publish_client.rs`'s `classify_cargo_output`/`classify_npm_publish_output`/etc.) is to check `output.success()` and return a descriptive `Err` on failure — not to silently degrade to a partial-success report.
- A git staging failure after manifests already wrote to disk is an actionable, surprising failure (hook rejection, permissions, disk issues) that the caller needs to see immediately as a hard error (surfaced through `CliError`) rather than have it swallowed into a report that claims success. Given nothing currently branches on `.staged` for control flow, returning `Err` is strictly safer and no more disruptive than a "partial" outcome that nobody reads.

**Fix**: both call sites now do `let output = runner.run("git", &args, root)?;` (propagates spawn/IO errors via `?`) followed by an explicit `if !output.success() { return Err(GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed { program: "git".into(), exit_code: output.exit_code, stderr: output.stderr })); }`.

- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, deep sweep)

- **Fix Status**: unfixed, not yet dispatched.

```rust
fn resolve_since<R: CommandRunner>(
    repo: Option<&callisto_vcs::GitRepository>,
    runner: &R,
    root: &Path,
    tag_name: &str,
) -> Option<CommitSha> {
    if let Some(r) = repo {
        if let Ok(sha) = r.resolve_commit(tag_name) {
            return sha;
        }
    }
    let rev = format!("{tag_name}^{{commit}}");
    let output = runner.run("git", &["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", &rev], root).ok()?;
    if !output.success() { return None; }
    let sha_str = output.stdout_trimmed();
    if sha_str.is_empty() { return None; }
    CommitSha::parse(sha_str).ok()
}
```

- If a `GitRepository` was discovered and `resolve_commit` returns `Ok(_)` (even `Ok(None)` for a genuinely missing tag), that result is authoritative and returned immediately — the `CommandRunner` is never touched. This preserves the pre-existing `test_aggregate_resolves_since_without_shelling_through_runner` test, which asserts a `PoisonedRunner` (always errors) must not break `since` resolution when gix is available.
- Only when `repo` is `None` (permanently the case on `wasm32`, since gix is excluded there) or the discovered repo's `resolve_commit` itself errors, it falls back to `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <tag>^{commit}` via `CommandRunner`, matching the pre-gix-unification approach.

**Bug**: `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`'s `fetch_commits` discarded its `CommandRunner` parameter (`_runner`) and hard-failed via `?` on `GitRepository::discover(cwd)` with no fallback — on wasm32 (where gix is compiled out and `discover` always returns `Err`), this silently dropped all conventional-commit severity inference, since the caller in `aggregate()` wraps the call in `if let Ok(...)`.

**Fix design** (`crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`):
- `fetch_commits` now tries gix first (`GitRepository::discover` → `commits_since_with_pathspec`) using the same `if let Ok(...) { if let Ok(...) { return ... } }` fall-through shape as `callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`'s `fetch_all_tags` and `changed.rs`'s `changed_since_last_tag` — never `?` on the gix path, so any gix failure (not just `discover`) falls through to the runner fallback.
- New `fetch_commits_via_command_runner` shells out: `git log --no-merges --format=<RS>%H<US>%B <range> [-- <pathspecs>]`.
  - `--no-merges` mirrors the gix path's `info.parent_ids().count() > 1` skip.
  - Range is `<since>..HEAD` for `SinceCommit` (exclusive lower bound, matching the revwalk's stop-at-`since`) or bare `HEAD` for `FullHistory`.
  - Trailing `-- <pathspecs>` reproduces `git log`'s own pathspec-prefix filtering.
- **Format string**: `--format=\x1e%H\x1f%B` — record separator (`\x1e`, ASCII RS) prefixes each record, unit separator (`\x1f`, ASCII US) splits sha from the raw message body (`%B`, git's unwrapped subject+blank+body, structurally equivalent to the gix path's `summary + "\n\n" + body` reconstruction). These control characters can't plausibly appear in commit text, so multi-line messages can never be misparsed as extra records/fields. Deliberately avoided `git log -z` (NUL-terminated, cleaner) because it requires git ≥2.34, newer than the workspace's declared `>=2.20` floor (`callisto_model::exec::REQUIRED_GIT`). Parsing strips the one trailing `\n` that `tformat:`-style `--format=` output appends per entry, then `split_once(FIELD_SEP)`; a missing separator or unparseable 40-hex-char SHA now returns `ConventionalError::MalformedGitLogOutput` (a variant that existed but was previously dead code) instead of panicking or dropping the commit silently.

## Summary

**Design decision: option (b) — lazy `TagIndex` via `OnceCell`, graph stays eager.**

### Investigation findings
Grepping every command handler's use of `ws.graph`/`ws.tags` (both directly in `callisto-cli/src/commands/*.rs`, which mostly just forward `&ws` into `callisto_graph::commands::*`, and inside that module where the real consumption happens) showed:
- `ws.graph` is needed by nearly everything: `publish`, `snapshot`, `status`, `tag`, `validate`, `version`, `pr_body` (transitively via `version`), and `add`'s interactive path (package names only).
- `ws.tags` is needed by a strictly smaller set: `publish`, `status`, `tag`, `version` (and `pr_body` transitively). It is **not** needed by `init`, `snapshot`, `validate`, or either of `add`'s paths.
- `add`'s non-interactive path uses only `ws.root`; its interactive path uses only `ws.graph.packages()` names.

### Why (b) over (a)
`TagIndex::build`'s only inputs (`runner`, `root`, `graph`, `config`) are already fields on `Workspace` itself, so deferring it behind a `OnceCell` needed zero new state and is transparent to every existing caller — a pure, no-downside win for `init`, both `add` paths, `snapshot`, and `validate` today, and for any future tag-agnostic command. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (the graph), by contrast, needs an external `locator: &L` that `Workspace` doesn't currently store; making it lazy too would require broadening `Workspace`'s generic/lifetime surface for a benefit that (per the grep) only helps 2 of ~10 command paths. `Workspace` was already using `RefCell` for interior mutability (`manifest_cache`) and is always accessed via `&Workspace` (never `&mut`), so `OnceCell` fit the existing ownership pattern cleanly with no `unsafe`/no new lifetime plumbing. Also relevant: this codebase's own comments treat `CommandRunner`/git round-trips as the expensive thing to avoid (explicitly, re: wasm32 Extism guest↔host round-trips), more so than in-process manifest parsing — reinforcing that `TagIndex`'s `git tag --list` fallback was the higher-value target to eliminate.

### Implementation
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`: `Workspace.tags` changed from `TagIndex` to `OnceCell<TagIndex>`; `Workspace::load` no longer calls `TagIndex::build` eagerly; added `Workspace::tags(&self) -> Result<&TagIndex, GraphError>` that builds-and-caches on first call.
- Updated all 6 direct-field call sites to `ws.tags()?`: `commands/status.rs`, `commands/version.rs`, `commands/tag.rs` (×2), `commands/publish.rs` (×2).
- Updated 8 test-fixture `Workspace { .. }` struct literals in `tests/graph_tests.rs` to `tags: OnceCell::from(tags)`.
- `add.rs` itself required **no changes** — its non-interactive path already only touched `ws.root`, so it benefits automatically now that `Workspace::load` no longer forces tag-index construction.

### TDD evidence
New test: `crates/callisto-graph/tests/tags_laziness_test.rs`, a `CommandRunner` double counting `git tag --list` invocations on a non-git-discoverable root (forces the `CommandRunner` fallback deterministically).
- **Red**: temporarily reverted just the `Workspace`/`lib.rs` change back to the eager-field shape and re-ran `cargo test -p callisto-graph --test tags_laziness_test` → compile failure (`no method named 'tags' found for reference '&Workspace<...>'; field, not a method`) across all 6 call sites — proving the pre-fix code can't satisfy the test.
- **Green**: restored the fix, re-ran → `test workspace_load_does_not_build_tag_index_until_tags_is_called ... ok`, asserting 0 `git tag --list` calls after `Workspace::load`, exactly 1 after the first `ws.tags()`, still 1 after a second call.

I also attempted a CLI-process-level end-to-end test for `add.rs` (a fake `git` on `PATH` logging invocations), but dropped it: it required `unsafe { std::env::set_var(...) }`, which conflicts with this repo's workspace-wide `unsafe_code = "forbid"` lint (inherited by `callisto-cli`). The Workspace-level test is the sound, safe proof and directly exercises the mechanism `add.rs` depends on.

### Final verification
- `cargo test -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli`: all green — 74 lib unit tests, 18+3+1+1 integration test files (`graph_tests`, `init_reconcile_test`, `manifest_cache_test`, `tags_laziness_test`), 6 e2e/lifecycle tests, 1 trycmd test, doctests — 0 failures.
- `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli`: clean.
- No remaining direct `ws.tags` field accesses anywhere in the repo (verified by grep) — every call site now goes through the accessor.

**File**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`

### Investigation — real call sites found

I grepped the workspace for every place a `Version`-bearing struct is deserialized via serde (not via ecosystem-aware `Version::parse`/`VersionReq::parse`):

- `crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs` — `CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish` (all `#[derive(Deserialize)]`, `version: Version`), part of `PublishPlan`.
- `crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs` — `PublishAttempt`, `BumpRecord`, `StatusPackageRecord` etc., all `#[derive(Deserialize)]` with `Version` fields, part of `PublishReport`/`VersionReport`/`StatusReport`.
- **The only cross-process/file-boundary deserialization of any of these** is `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/tag.rs:31`: `let plan: PublishPlan = serde_json::from_str(&plan_text)`. This reads a `PublishPlan` from a file or stdin — i.e. a plan produced by an earlier `plan-publish --format json` invocation, potentially in a different process/CI step, so nothing in that call site's context (no sibling `Ecosystem`/`VersionGrammar` field — only `RegistryKey`, a string) can supply a grammar hint. This is exactly the "no other grammar signal available" case the task asked me to look for.

I then checked whether that call site can *actually* carry a PEP-440 `Version` today. It cannot, currently: `plan_publish()` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs` only branches on `PublishTarget::CratesIo` and `PublishTarget::Npm{..}` when populating `rust_crates`/`npm_platform_packages`/`npm_main_packages`; there is no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch, and `ReleaseEntry` (the only place a Pypi-only package would land) has no `version` field. So no PEP-440 `Version` reaches this deserialization path today.

However, PyPI/PEP 440 is not a stub ecosystem: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs` fully parses `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg` versions as PEP 440, `crates/callisto-format/src/bump.rs` implements PEP-440 bump logic, and `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs` has a fully implemented, heavily tested `pypi_publish` (twine upload, already-published/rate-limit/auth-failure classification). `Ecosystem::Pypi.is_implemented()` is `true`. The PyPI registry-client work is done; only the `plan_publish` → `PublishPlan` wiring for PyPI packages is missing — a closely related, separate gap. The moment that wiring is added (a natural next step for this actively-developed ecosystem), `tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` deserialization becomes silently broken for exactly the PEP-440-only version strings the existing "gap 9" pinning test already demonstrated fail.

### Decision

Given a real, generic-serde-only call site exists (`tag.rs` plan ingestion) with no available grammar signal, and PEP 440/PyPI is a live, non-stub grammar in this codebase, I implemented the same multi-grammar-fallback pattern `VersionReq::deserialize` already uses (Cargo → Npm → Pypi), applied to `Version::deserialize`: try `VersionGrammar::SemVer` first (strictest, most unambiguous), fall back to `VersionGrammar::Pep440` only if SemVer fails. The residual ambiguity — a string valid under both grammars (e.g. `1.2.3`) always resolves to SemVer — is documented directly on the `Deserialize` impl, mirroring how `VersionReq`'s chain accepts the same tradeoff, and is pinned by a new test.

### Implementation

- `Version::deserialize` now does `Version::parse(&s, VersionGrammar::SemVer).or_else(|_| Version::parse(&s, VersionGrammar::Pep440))`, with a doc comment explaining the rationale, the SemVer-preferred ambiguity tradeoff, and pointing callers with known grammar context to `Version::parse` directly.
- Updated the former "gap 9" pinning test (`version_deserialize_is_hardcoded_to_semver_and_rejects_pep440_only_strings`) to `version_deserialize_falls_back_to_pep440_for_pep440_only_strings`, now asserting successful round-trip with `VersionGrammar::Pep440` recovered.
- Added two new tests: rejection when a string is invalid under both grammars, and confirmation that SemVer wins when a string is valid under both.

### Test results

`cargo test -p callisto-model -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli`: all green — 34 tests in `callisto-model` (including the 3 version-deserialize tests), 74+16+1 in `callisto-graph`, 2+4+2+1+6 across `callisto-cli` suites, 0 failures. `cargo clippy --all-targets` on the same three crates: clean, no warnings.

Found the same pattern again — two more real gaps, not yet in the ledger:

- **`callisto pre enter`/`callisto pre exit`** — `--dry-run` is never referenced anywhere in `pre.rs`. Writes `.changeset/pre.json` unconditionally.
- **`callisto init`** — `InitOptions` doesn't even have a `dry_run` field. `--dry-run --yes` together still writes `callisto.toml` to disk.

**Why this keeps happening**: it's pure convention today, not structure. `atomic_write` itself (the shared primitive underneath almost every write) has zero dry-run awareness — no parameter, no gate. `ApplyOptions.transient` is the one place a real shared gate exists, and it works well (`version`/`snapshot` can't forget, because they route through it and it's checked twice inside `apply_version_plan`) — but it only covers that one pipeline. `tag.rs` correctly reinvented an equivalent independently. `pre.rs`/`init.rs` just never added anything. And there's no generic test — coverage is per-command and reactive, added only after each bug was already found, which is exactly why these two survived undetected.

Two ways to actually fix "how do we make sure," different tradeoffs:

1. **Push dry-run-awareness into the write primitives themselves** — make `atomic_write` (and the `GitDataSource` write methods) require an explicit write-authorization value derived once from `global.dry_run`, so it's structurally impossible to reach a real write without having threaded the flag through. This is the real fix — it doesn't just catch the bug, it makes the bug class hard to write in the first place. Cost: `atomic_write`'s signature is used broadly, so this touches every caller across `callisto-manifests`/`callisto-changelog`/`callisto-graph`.
2. **A generic cross-command regression test** — one test that runs every write-capable command under `--dry-run` and asserts zero filesystem/git mutation, repo-wide, instead of the current per-command reactive tests. Cheap, catches future regressions, but doesn't prevent the bug from being written — only detects it after the fact (still requires someone to run the suite).

I'd do both — (1) as the real fix, (2) as the safety net in case a future write mechanism bypasses `atomic_write`/`GitDataSource` entirely (e.g. a raw `fs::write` someone adds later). Given (1) is a signature change touching every `atomic_write` caller, want me to scope and dispatch both now, or start with the two concrete bugs (`pre.rs`, `init.rs`) plus the regression test, and treat the primitive-level redesign as its own follow-up given its wider blast radius?

content.text:
## Research findings

**The capability-token pattern is real, proven, and directly fits — but even cargo itself doesn't do this**, which is the most useful data point. Cargo's `--dry-run` is a bare `bool` threaded by convention through `ops::registry::publish`, and its own bug tracker has open issues (#14249, #11514) that are exactly this bug class — a dry-run silently diverging from real behavior because some call site forgot the check, in a flagship, heavily-reviewed Rust project, a decade after the flag shipped. That's strong evidence "remember to check the bool" fails even under scrutiny, and validates not settling for convention here.

Two real patterns compose into the right answer:
1. **Terraform's plan/apply separation** — compute an immutable plan independent of dry-run status; "decide what to do" and "do it" are different functions with different signatures. Callisto already has a partial version of this (`VersionPlan`/`apply_version_plan`) — it should become the universal shape, not the exception.
2. **A capability-token type** (the PermRust/typestate pattern — real, used in security-sensitive Rust code, e.g. `oauth2-rs`, embedded HAL pin typestates) — a zero-sized `ApplyPermit` that only one `dry_run`-aware constructor can mint from `GlobalArgs`, required as a parameter by every side-effecting primitive (`atomic_write`, `GitDataSource::create_tag`, git staging). Not calling the check becomes a compile error, not a runtime bug. No off-the-shelf crate exists for this — it's legitimately hand-rolled territory in the Rust ecosystem, but the pattern itself is proven.

Backed by a shared `assert_fs`-based test helper (the standard Rust CLI testing tool for this) that snapshots the workspace tree before/after any `--dry-run` invocation and asserts equality — applied uniformly, replacing the current per-command reactive tests.

**Other properties that deserve the same global treatment** — ranked by how real/stark the gap is:

1. **Logging/verbosity** — starkest gap. Zero logging infrastructure anywhere (no `tracing`/`log`, no `-v` flag, no dependency). The only non-report output is one `eprintln!` on fatal error. No way to ask "why did this happen" short of reading source.
2. **Exit code convention** — genuinely inconsistent. `status` has a real 3-way convention (`SUCCESS`/`FAILURE`/`2` for pending-changes-under---check); everything else is binary, so `version --strict`/`validate --strict` have no way to distinguish "hard error" from "strict-mode escalation" for scripting.
3. **CI/non-interactive detection** — `add.rs` and `init.rs` each independently reinvent the same `stdin().is_terminal()` one-liner. No shared `GlobalArgs` helper, no `$CI` check.
4. **Confirmation/`--yes`** — narrower gap: only `init` has it. `publish` (irreversible registry uploads) has no prompt and no `--yes` at all — arguably the highest-stakes command has the weakest "are you sure."
5. **`--strict`/`--strict-graph` on mutating commands** — `snapshot`/`tag`/`publish` have none, though they can hit graph/diagnostic warnings today with no way to escalate to failure.
6. Audit trail — lower priority, more of a product decision than missing plumbing.

## Proposed solution

You are implementing a structural fix in the callisto Rust repo at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto so that forgetting to check `--dry-run` before a filesystem/git write becomes a compile error instead of a silent bug. This is real architecture work — be thoughtful, this is the biggest structural change of the session so far. Standing constraints: NEVER run git commit. NEVER bump versions or run release/publish commands. TDD throughout.

## Background

Two confirmed, currently-unfixed bugs motivate this: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs` (`pre enter`/`pre exit`) and `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs`/`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/init.rs` both write to disk unconditionally, never checking `global.dry_run` at all — the same bug class as two already-fixed bugs (`version --dry-run`, `add --dry-run`), now found a third and fourth time. Research this session (cargo's own `--dry-run` bug tracker — issues #14249, #11514 — shows this exact bug class persists even in flagship, heavily-reviewed Rust projects when enforcement is just "remember to check a bool") concluded the fix should be a capability-token pattern: a value that must be obtained before a write function can be called at all, so the check can't be silently omitted by a new command or a new write path in an existing one.

## Design to implement

**1. `ApplyPermit` type, in `crates/callisto-model`** (Layer 1 — already the common dependency of `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-vcs`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto-cli`, so this is the correct home; verify against `AGENTS.md`'s layer table that this doesn't violate anything before proceeding):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ApplyPermit { _private: () }

impl ApplyPermit {
    /// The one sanctioned construction path: mint a permit unless dry-run was requested.
    /// Call sites should derive `dry_run` directly from `GlobalArgs`, not recompute it.
    pub fn granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run: bool) -> Option<Self> {
        if dry_run { None } else { Some(Self { _private: () }) }
    }

    /// Test-only escape hatch, named loudly so any non-test usage is obvious in review/grep.
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-util"))]
    pub fn force_for_tests() -> Self { Self { _private: () } }
}
```

Adjust naming/shape if you find a cleaner idiom while implementing, but preserve the core property: the only way to get a real `ApplyPermit` outside tests is via `granted_unless_dry_run`, and it must be threaded as an explicit parameter into every side-effecting function below — never optional, never defaulted, never inferred.

**2. Require `&ApplyPermit` in every write primitive:**
- `crates/callisto-manifests/src/atomic.rs`'s `atomic_write` (and `ChangesetStorage`'s trait method if it has one) — add `permit: &ApplyPermit` as a required parameter.
- `crates/callisto-vcs`'s `GitDataSource` trait's `create_tag`/`create_floating_major` methods (both the `GitRepository` and `ShellGit` implementations, from this session's earlier trait consolidation) — add `permit: &ApplyPermit`.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`'s git staging calls (`git add`/`git rm --cached`) — require `&ApplyPermit` in whatever function wraps them.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`'s `SubprocessRegistryClient::publish` (the actual `cargo publish`/`npm publish`/`twine upload` calls — the highest-stakes writes in the whole codebase) — require `&ApplyPermit` too. `is_published` (read-only) does not need one.

**3. Update every caller across the workspace** to obtain `Option<ApplyPermit>` from `global.dry_run` once, near the top of each command handler, and branch: `None` → compute and report/preview what would happen, call zero write primitives; `Some(permit)` → proceed with real writes, passing `&permit` through. This is mechanical for already-correct commands (`version.rs`/`snapshot.rs` via `apply.rs`, `add.rs`, `tag.rs`, `publish.rs`) — thread the permit through their existing dry-run branches. For the two currently-broken commands, this requires real new work:
   - `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs`: add the missing `global.dry_run` check entirely — preview what `.changeset/pre.json` would contain/become (mirror the output shape `add.rs`'s dry-run preview uses: both text and JSON formats) without writing, when dry-run; obtain a real permit and write when not.
   - `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/init.rs` / `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs`: add `dry_run` handling alongside the existing `--yes`/reconcile-diff logic from earlier this session (these are two independent gates — `--dry-run` must prevent ALL three write sites regardless of `--yes`; today `--yes --dry-run` together still writes, fix that combination specifically and add a test for it).

**4. Shared dry-run regression test helper**, in `crates/callisto-fixtures` (the existing shared test-support crate from this session's earlier consolidation work): using `assert_fs` (add as a dev-dependency if not already present — check first), a helper that snapshots a workspace directory tree (file paths + content hashes, not mtimes, to avoid false positives) before and after a closure runs, and asserts equality. Apply this generically across every write-capable command (`add`, `version`, `snapshot`, `pre` enter/exit, `init`, `tag`, `publish`) invoked with `--dry-run`/an equivalent `ApplyPermit::None` path — replacing or supplementing the current per-command ad hoc dry-run tests with this shared, uniform invariant. This is what would have caught the `pre.rs`/`init.rs` bugs immediately instead of leaving them undiscovered.

## TDD requirements

For the two real bugs (`pre.rs`, `init.rs`): write the shared regression-test helper first, run it against current code for `pre enter`/`pre exit`/`init`, confirm it fails (real file mutation detected under `--dry-run`), then implement the fix, confirm it passes. For the signature-change propagation across already-correct commands: the existing test suites for those commands must stay green throughout — if a test needs updating because it directly asserted the old signature shape (e.g. calling `atomic_write` with the old arg count), update it to match, don't weaken the assertion.

## Scope discipline

This touches many files — stay disciplined about not changing behavior anywhere it was already correct (`version`/`snapshot`/`add`/`tag`/`publish`'s actual dry-run semantics should be unchanged, only their internal plumbing now requires a permit). Do not add the broader `tracing`/logging, exit-code-convention, or CI-detection work discussed in the wider proposal — that's explicitly out of scope for this task, a separate future wave.

Run `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` and confirm everything passes. Report back: the final `ApplyPermit` design (adjust from the sketch if you found a better shape, explain why), the full list of signature changes and files touched, the failing-test evidence for the `pre.rs`/`init.rs` fixes specifically (before/after), confirmation that `--yes --dry-run` together on `init` no longer writes, and final workspace-wide test results.

- `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` — single factory that tries gix then falls back to ShellGit

You are fixing a confirmed bug in the Callisto Rust workspace at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto.

## The Bug (Track E)

`PackageId::matches` in `crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs` has this implementation:

```rust
pub fn matches(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
    if self == other { return true; }
    if self.name() == other.name() {
        match (self.ecosystem(), other.ecosystem()) {
            (None, _) | (_, None) => true,   // <-- the problem
            (Some(e1), Some(e2)) => e1 == e2,
        }
    } else {
        false
    }
}
```

`(None, _) | (_, None) => true` means a `Bare("foo")` matches BOTH `Prefixed(Cargo, "foo")` AND `Prefixed(Npm, "foo")` simultaneously. In a graph containing both, a bare lookup silently matches both packages — an ambiguity that should be an error.

## What's already in place

`aggregate.rs`'s `resolve_target_package` already handles the multi-match case correctly: it collects all `.matches()` results, and returns `Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName)` if there are 2+. So the graph layer correctly surfaces the error — the bug is that `matches()` itself is semantically misleading: `Bare("foo").matches(Prefixed(Npm, "foo"))` returns `true` even though a bare ID isn't a claim that the package is from npm. The current behavior is "could be the same package" — the intended behavior should be "is definitely the same package."

1. `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:152` — `packages.filter(|p| p.id.matches(id)).collect()` in `resolve_target_package`. This collects ALL matches and errors on ambiguity — ALREADY CORRECT, relies on `matches()` to mean "could be."
2. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs:87` — `ws.graph.packages().any(|p| p.id.matches(&id))`. This checks existence only — bare name is treated as "package exists in any ecosystem."

Clean history. 10 commits, working tree has only the `.changeset/` directory left (which is runtime output, not committed). 

The log tells the full story in order: VCS layer → PEP 440 fixes → ApplyPermit → dry-run enforcement → graph improvements → publish orchestrator → CLI/moon → tests → docs → cleanup.
What's left to fix and implement in regards to bugs and gaps? Python support?

Here's the honest current state:

**Remaining CLI correctness gaps (second wave, no bugs dispatched yet):**
- `add.rs` and `init.rs` each independently reinvent `stdin().is_terminal()` — should be one function
- Exit-code convention is inconsistent (`status` returns a 3-way code, everything else is binary)
- No `-v`/`--verbose` flag or `tracing` infrastructure anywhere
- `--strict`/`--strict-graph` missing from `snapshot`, `tag`, `publish`
- `publish` has no `--yes` confirmation gate — the highest-stakes command has the weakest guard

**Python support — four distinct gaps, in priority order:**

1. **Dependency-constraint rewriting** — `round_trip()` in `callisto-manifests` has no `Pypi` arm. Without it, a `callisto version` bump updates `pyproject.toml`'s own version but silently leaves `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` / `[project.dependencies]` pointing at the old range. This is a correctness bug for any Python monorepo with inter-package deps.

2. **PEP 735 dependency groups** — `04-python-engine-spec.md` asserts support; zero code exists. Either implement or remove the claim from the spec. Current state is a doc lie.

3. **Workspace discovery** — no support for `uv.workspace` or Poetry workspace configs. Needs a design decision (explicit config in `callisto.toml` vs. auto-detection) before implementation.

4. **Publishing** — `PublishTarget::Pypi` variant exists in `callisto-model` but the publish orchestrator has no match arm for it. `twine upload --skip-existing` is the right mechanism (already researched).

**Go — spec only, no code.** The spec doesn't cover import-path propagation to internal importers or how a changeset maps onto Go's tag-only versioning model. Not implementable without a spec extension first.

**Deferred by design:**
- `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml` publish cutover — one registry at a time, when you're ready to shadow-test against a real low-stakes publish
- `WorkspaceCargoResolver` BOM write path — flagged as unverified but not yet reproduced as a real failure

The most impactful next item is **Python `round_trip`** — it's a real silent correctness gap in an otherwise working Python ecosystem. Want to scope and dispatch that first, or tackle the CLI second-wave?
Is there a way to dispatch succesfully addressing it all with the most appropriate models and effort? Let's consider doc updates, rsdoc, testing, etc in a workflow

How can we best do this? Think through it, research, reason and plan

Good analysis from Gemini. Let me think through this carefully against our specific codebase before proposing anything.

---

**Gate 1 (OS & Spec Boundary Matrix)** — Partially right, but over-broad

Windows backslash/POSIX is real but lower-stakes for Callisto specifically: moon extensions run on Linux/macOS CI, and the pathspec matching in `vcs/lib.rs` (Bug 14) only affects `git log` filtering. Worth fixing, but it's not a blocker. The genuinely actionable part of this gate is **2-part PEP 440 versions** and **BOM on WorkspaceCargoResolver**. The real fix is centralizing — not matrix-testing in isolation.

**Gate 2 (proptest everywhere)** — Right idea, wrong scope

"All parsing and manifest writing functions" is unworkable. Proptest is valuable for pure domain functions with bounded input spaces: `Version`, `DepSpec`, `PackageId`, `round_trip`. It's wasteful for file I/O wrappers. We already use proptest in `identity.rs` and `version.rs` — we should extend it to `round_trip` functions and the bump functions, not spray it everywhere.

**Gate 3 (CLI exit code assertions)** — Correct and underdone

Bug 20 (publish exits 0 on failure) is a direct consequence of zero integration tests asserting failure exit codes. This is the most mechanically fixable gate — `trycmd` / `assert_cmd` already exist in the codebase and handle this natively.

**Gate 4 (single-trait centralization)** — Half done, half premature

`atomic_write` is already centralized (Track G). BOM stripping is the remaining real duplication — it's done in `cargo.rs`/`npm.rs`/`python.rs` independently, and `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load` missed it entirely (Bug 17). The fix is `callisto-manifests::common::strip_bom()` called by every parser, not a new trait. Adding `CstManifestEditor` / `DurableStorage` traits on top of the existing `Manifest` trait would add abstraction without removing duplication.

---

**My concrete plan:**

**Tier 1 — Code changes that prevent entire classes of bugs:**

1. **Centralize BOM stripping in `common.rs`** — already exists as a file, just needs a `pub fn strip_bom(s: &str) -> &str` that all TOML/JSON parsers call. Fixes Bug 17, prevents recurrence pattern-wide.

2. **Normalize pathspec matching to POSIX** in `vcs/lib.rs` `location_matches` — one `str::replace('\\', "/")` call on the spec side. Fixes Bug 14.

3. **Extend proptest to `round_trip` and `bump`** — add generators for `Version` (1-part, 2-part, 3-part, pre-release variants) and `DepSpec` to `callisto-fixtures`, then property-test `round_trip(spec, bumped) != None` for recognized forms and `bump(v) > v` always. These catch the 2-part version bug class entirely.

4. **Add `AGENTS.md` Invariant 6: Mandatory Input Boundaries** — any function touching version strings, file content, or paths must have explicit tests for: BOM-prefixed content, CRLF line endings, 2-part versions, paths with only `.` components. This gates future agent work at the doc level.

**Tier 2 — Test infrastructure that catches regressions:**

5. **Exit code integration test suite** — a `tests/exit_codes.rs` in `callisto-cli` using `assert_cmd` that covers: every command's success → 0, every command's error → 1, `publish` with a failing mock runner → 1, `status` clean → 2, `status` with changesets → 0.

6. **Proptest round-trip property for manifests** — `parse(write(parse(content))) == parse(content)` for `CargoToml`, `PackageJson`, `PyprojectToml`. This catches the BOM/CRLF restoration bugs before they ship.

**Tier 3 — Architectural enforcement (lighter than Gemini suggests):**

7. Update `AGENTS.md` to make Invariants 1-5 more explicit about what they cover, and add a "Test Matrix" checklist table that agents must verify for any new parser or version-handling function.

---

**What I'd skip from Gemini's proposal:**

- Formal `CstManifestEditor` / `DurableStorage` traits — the existing `Manifest` trait is the right abstraction, adding another layer adds complexity without removing duplication
- proptest on file I/O wrappers — too much ceremony for code that's already exercised by integration tests
- Full Windows CI matrix — valid eventually, not yet: we don't claim Windows support, and adding a Windows runner costs CI budget before the target is even stated

---

**Sequencing:**

I'm still waiting on the two bug verification reports (Gemini's 20 bugs). Once those land I want to dispatch a single fix batch covering all confirmed bugs + Tier 1+2 above in parallel agents. Want me to proceed that way, or adjust the scope first?

input.prompt:
You are researching real-world polyglot monorepo patterns to identify concrete test cases for Callisto, a versioning tool that manages SemVer/PEP 440 bumps across Rust, npm, and Python packages in a single monorepo.

## What to research (read-only, no code changes)

### 1. napi-rs pattern (Rust → Node.js native addon)

napi-rs is the dominant pattern for shipping Rust as a Node.js native addon. Research what the version coupling looks like:

- Read https://github.com/nicolo-ribaudo/tc39-proposal-async-iterator-helpers/blob/main/package.json if accessible, or instead look at the napi-rs template at https://github.com/napi-rs/package-template
- Key questions: When a Rust crate version bumps, does the npm package version bump too? How is the dependency expressed in package.json — is it `optionalDependencies` to platform-specific packages, or a direct dep on the Rust crate output?
- What does the workspace structure look like? Is Cargo.toml at the root or in a subdirectory?

### 2. Real Rust + Python examples (maturin/PyO3)

Maturin builds Python wheels from Rust source. Research:
- The Polars project structure: `py-polars/pyproject.toml` depends on `polars` (the Rust crate output). What version format do they use? Is it exact pin `==X.Y.Z` or range `>=X.Y.Z`?
- The `cryptography` Python package (pyca/cryptography) which uses Rust internally — how does its pyproject.toml reference the Rust version?
- The `pydantic-core` project: Rust + Python in a monorepo. How is versioning coordinated?
- Key question: When a Rust core version bumps, what constraint format do the Python bindings use to track it?

### 3. Turborepo / moonrepo patterns (Rust CLI + TypeScript workspace)

The moonrepo itself is a Rust CLI with TypeScript SDK packages. Research:
- How does the @moonrepo/sdk npm package version track the moon CLI Rust version?
- What does a typical `packages/*/package.json` look like in a repo that also has Cargo crates?
- Do they use `workspace:*` npm protocol for intra-repo JS deps?

### 4. SWC (Rust → npm) pattern

SWC compiles Rust to npm packages. The @swc/* namespace has many packages. Research:
- How many npm packages does a single Rust crate fork into?
- What does the version cascade look like — do all @swc/* packages share a version, or do they version independently?

### 5. Cross-language version constraint corner cases to synthesize

Based on the above research, identify the concrete input cases that a polyglot versioning tool must handle:

a) Package naming: Rust crates use `kebab-case`, npm uses `@scope/kebab-case`, Python uses `snake_case` on PyPI but `kebab-case` in package display names. What does cross-ecosystem matching on the "same logical package" look like?

b) Version format mismatches: Rust SemVer pre-releases use `-alpha.1` notation; PEP 440 uses `a1` or `1.0.0a1`. When a Rust crate publishes `1.0.0-alpha.1`, what should the Python binding's pyproject.toml constraint become?

c) npm `workspace:*` protocol: When packages inside an npm workspace reference each other with `"dep": "workspace:*"`, how should a version bump tool handle that constraint — leave it as `workspace:*`, or rewrite to `"dep": "^NEW_VERSION"`?

d) Cargo workspace inheritance: `version.workspace = true` in member Cargo.toml means the member inherits the workspace root version. When the workspace root version bumps, which members auto-inherit and which have their own version?

e) Platform-specific npm packages from napi-rs: A Rust crate `my-lib` produces `@scope/my-lib-linux-x64-gnu`, `@scope/my-lib-darwin-arm64`, etc. plus a `@scope/my-lib` wrapper. When the Rust version bumps, all N+1 npm packages must bump together. How should Callisto model this as a linked group?

Report concrete examples with actual version strings, constraint formats, and workspace structures you find. This will directly inform test fixtures for Callisto.

input.description: Fix CRLF changelog header corruption in write.rs
input.prompt:
TDD bug fix in a Rust codebase. Follow strict red-green-refactor: write the failing test first, confirm it fails, then implement the fix.

## Bug

File: `crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs`

`prepend()` uses `strip_prefix(&format!("# {display_name}\n\n"))` and `strip_prefix(&format!("# {display_name}\n"))` to locate and remove an existing heading before prepending new content. These patterns use LF-only line endings. A CRLF changelog (`"# pkg\r\n\r\n"`) does not match either pattern, so the code falls to the else branch and prepends the new entry ABOVE the existing header — displacing the heading on every run.

## Task

1. Read `crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` in full.
2. Add a failing test `prepend_does_not_displace_header_in_crlf_changelog` (or similar) inside the existing `#[cfg(test)]` block. The test should:
   - Build an existing CRLF changelog string: `"# My Package\r\n\r\n## 1.0.0\r\n\r\nSome content\r\n"`
   - Call `prepend("My Package", "## 1.1.0\n\nNew stuff\n", existing)` (or however the function signature looks — read the actual code)
   - Assert the result starts with `"# My Package"` (the header must be first, not second)
   - Assert the new section appears between the header and the old content

input.prompt:
Adversarial audit of the changelog generation subsystem in a Rust monorepo versioning tool called Callisto. Read-only — find bugs, do not edit files.

## Scope

Focus entirely on changelog generation. The relevant code is in:
- `crates/callisto-changelog/src/` — all files (write.rs, render.rs, or whatever's there)
- `crates/callisto-conventional/src/` — commit parsing that feeds into changelog content
- Any callers that invoke changelog generation (look in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs` or similar)

## What to look for

**Correctness bugs:**
1. Does the generated markdown format match the expected structure? Look for heading level errors (e.g. `##` vs `###`), missing blank lines, or malformed anchor links that would cause renderers to produce incorrect HTML.
2. Edge cases in commit grouping: what happens when a commit has BOTH a scope AND is breaking? Does the section heading correctly reflect both? What if breaking is true but the commit type is `fix` (not `feat`)?
3. What happens when multiple packages share the same changeset file? Is each package's section generated independently, or is there any state bleed between packages?
4. What if a changeset's summary field is empty? What if it contains markdown special chars like `*`, `_`, `[`, `]`, `#`?
5. What if a changeset's summary has a trailing newline or leading whitespace? Does the rendered output look broken?
6. What if a package has zero changesets but is bumped because it's in a linked group (cascade bump)? Does it get a changelog section? Should it? (A cascade-only bump with no associated changesets might produce an empty `### Patch Changes` section or be silently omitted — either could be wrong.)
7. Version ordering: if a CHANGELOG.md already has entries for versions `1.2.0`, `1.1.0`, `1.0.0` (newest first), and we're adding `1.3.0`, does the new entry land at the top? Check `prepend()` against various existing-content shapes.
8. The `extract_section` function (if it exists): what happens when a version appears twice in the changelog? What if the version heading format uses a different number of `#` than what extract_section searches for?

**Data integrity bugs:**
9. Is the rendered changelog entry deduplicated? If two changesets both touch package A, do both summaries appear, or is one dropped?
10. Git breaking-change footer: `BREAKING CHANGE: description` — is the description used verbatim in the changelog? What if it's multi-line?
11. What happens if the package display name contains special markdown characters (e.g. `@scope/pkg-name` with a slash, or a name with backticks)?

**Integration bugs:**
12. Is the changeset filename included anywhere in the rendered output (it shouldn't be — it's internal)?
13. Does the changelog writer handle the case where `.changeset/` directory doesn't exist at all?
14. Concurrent writes: if two packages are being versioned at the same time (parallel apply), could two changelog writes interleave and corrupt each other's file?

For each finding: give the file path, line number(s), the exact failure scenario (what inputs cause it), and severity. Distinguish CONFIRMED (definitely wrong code path exists) from PLAUSIBLE (code path exists but unclear if reachable in practice).

content.text:
Yes, Callisto generates per-package `CHANGELOG.md` files — and the audit just found something alarming.

**The critical finding**: `agg.changelog_inputs` is populated by `aggregate()` with all the real changeset summaries, but `plan_version()` in `version.rs:107-124` **never reads it**. Instead it hardcodes `summary: "Release update"` and `filename: "changeset.md"` for every package on every run. Your actual changeset text is silently discarded and replaced with a placeholder. The e2e test only checks that the version number appears in the changelog, not the summary — so this has gone undetected.

Full findings ranked by severity:

| # | Severity | Bug |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical** | `changelog_inputs` never consumed — all changelogs say `"Release update"` |
| 2 | **High** | Multiple changesets per package collapsed to one hardcoded entry (data loss) |
| 3 | **High** | Cascade/group-bumped packages get `"Release update"` instead of a cascade note |
| 4 | **High** | Latent crash once #1 is fixed: cascade-only packages have empty entries → `EmptyInput` |
| 5 | **Medium** | Multi-line summaries produce broken markdown (continuation lines not indented 2 spaces) |
| 6 | **Medium** | Empty summary emits `"- \n"` with no guard |
| 7 | **Medium** | H1 header silently dropped if package `display_name()` differs from existing file header |
| 8 | **Low** | `extract_section` returns only first block when a version appears twice |
| 9 | **Low** | TOCTOU race if two packages share one changelog path |

---

**On a combined monorepo changelog**: not currently implemented. Each package gets its own file. A root-level aggregated changelog (like `@changesets/cli`'s `CHANGELOG.md` at the repo root listing all packages that changed in each release) is a reasonable feature — but right now the per-package changelogs don't even have the right content, so that's a good thing to tackle after fixing the critical bug.

Want me to dispatch agents to fix these? The critical `changelog_inputs` wire-up plus bugs 4, 5, and 6 are all related and likely need to be addressed together in one agent since they're in the same call chain.
Address all of them comprehensively
Three parallel agents — the data pipeline (bugs 1–4 are one tightly coupled fix), the renderer (bugs 5–6), and the writer (bugs 7–9).

input.prompt:
TDD bug fix in a Rust codebase (Callisto). Strict red-green-refactor — failing test before any production code change. Read the files before writing anything.

## Context

Callisto is a monorepo versioning tool. `aggregate()` builds `agg.changelog_inputs: BTreeMap<PackageId, ChangelogInput>` with real changeset summaries from `.changeset/*.md` files. `plan_version()` calls `aggregate()` but NEVER READS `agg.changelog_inputs` — it constructs a brand-new `ChangelogInput` for every bumped package with hardcoded `filename: "changeset.md"` and `summary: "Release update"`. All real changeset content is silently discarded.

## Files to read first

- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs` — the `plan_version` function (around lines 107–124)
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` — `aggregate()`, `union_fixed()`, `union_linked()`, and how `changelog_inputs` is populated
- `crates/callisto-changelog/src/render.rs` — `render_section()` and `ChangelogInput`/`ChangelogEntry` types  
- `crates/callisto-model/src/` — find where `ChangelogInput`, `ChangelogEntry`, `ChangeSource` are defined
- `crates/callisto-graph/tests/lifecycle_e2e_tests.rs` — see how the e2e test checks changelog content (it likely only checks version number, not summary text)

## Bugs to fix (all in the same data pipeline, must be addressed together)

**Bug 1 (Critical)**: `plan_version()` never reads `agg.changelog_inputs`. Every changelog says `"Release update"`.

**Bug 2 (High)**: Multiple changesets for the same package are collapsed to one entry because the hardcoded construction always creates `entries: vec![one_entry]`. After fixing Bug 1, this is automatically fixed since `agg.changelog_inputs` already accumulates all entries.

**Bug 3 (High)**: `union_fixed()` and `union_linked()` in `aggregate.rs` update `agg.severities` for cascade/group-bumped packages but never add any entry to `agg.changelog_inputs` for those packages. Packages bumped only by cascade or group propagation have no entry in `changelog_inputs` at all.

**Bug 4 (High, latent crash)**: After fixing Bug 1, if cascade-only packages have no entry in `changelog_inputs`, `plan_version()` will call `render_section()` with `entries: []`, which returns `Err(ChangelogError::EmptyInput)` and aborts the entire version application. So Bug 3 must be fixed at the same time: cascade-only packages need a synthetic `ChangelogEntry` with `ChangeSource::GroupUnion` (for fixed-group members) or `ChangeSource::DependencyUpdate` (for cascade bumps).

## Task

### Step 1: Write failing tests first

1a. In `crates/callisto-graph/tests/lifecycle_e2e_tests.rs` (or add a new `changelog_tests.rs` nearby), add a test that:
   - Creates a temporary workspace with at least one package having a `changelog` path configured
   - Writes a `.changeset/fix-foo.md` with a real summary like `"Fix the frobnication bug"`
   - Calls `plan_version()` (or runs the full pipeline if needed)
   - Asserts that the resulting `changelog_writes` (or the written CHANGELOG.md content) contains `"Fix the frobnication bug"`, NOT `"Release update"`

1b. Add a test for multiple changesets: two `.changeset/*.md` files both bumping the same package with different summaries — assert both summaries appear in the output (i.e. `entries.len() == 2`).

1c. If `plan_version()`'s return type includes `changelog_writes`, inspect it directly. Otherwise use the actual CHANGELOG.md written to a tempdir.

Run `cargo test -p callisto-graph -- changelog` (or similar filter) and confirm the tests fail.

### Step 2: Fix `plan_version()` in `version.rs`

Replace the hardcoded `ChangelogInput` construction with a lookup into `agg.changelog_inputs`. For packages that are in `agg.changelog_inputs`, use the real `ChangelogInput`. For packages that are bumped but have NO entry in `changelog_inputs` (cascade/group-only), create a synthetic `ChangelogInput` with one entry using `ChangeSource::GroupUnion` or `ChangeSource::DependencyUpdate` as appropriate — based on `agg.reasons` which already tracks whether the bump came from a cascade or group union.

Read `agg.reasons` to determine the right `ChangeSource` for cascade-only packages. The `ChangeSource` variants should be checked: look at `ChangeSource::GroupUnion { group_name }` and `ChangeSource::DependencyUpdate { dependency }` and use whichever matches the package's reason.

### Step 3: Fix `aggregate.rs` — populate `changelog_inputs` for cascade/group packages

In `union_fixed()` and `union_linked()`, when elevating a member's severity, also insert a synthetic `ChangelogEntry` into `agg.changelog_inputs[member_id]` with `source: ChangeSource::GroupUnion { group_name: group.name.clone() }` (or equivalent). Do the same in wherever cascade bumps are applied — add `ChangeSource::DependencyUpdate { dependency: dep_name }`.

Alternatively (and cleaner): after `aggregate()` finishes computing `severities`, make `plan_version()` itself synthesize entries for any package in `severities` that lacks an entry in `changelog_inputs`, using `agg.reasons` to pick the right `ChangeSource`. Either approach is acceptable as long as cascade-only packages have non-empty `entries`.

### Step 4: Update the e2e test

The e2e test at `lifecycle_e2e_tests.rs` likely only checks `changelog_content.contains("0.2.0")`. Add an assertion that checks the actual changeset summary text appears in the generated changelog.

### Step 5: Run full test suite

```
cargo test -p callisto-graph
cargo test -p callisto-changelog
cargo clippy -p callisto-graph -p callisto-changelog -- -D warnings
```

Confirm all tests pass and clippy is clean.

Do not commit. Leave all changes in the working tree.

input.prompt:
TDD bug fix in a Rust codebase (Callisto). Strict red-green-refactor — failing test before any production code change.

## Files to read first

- `crates/callisto-changelog/src/render.rs` — `render_section()` function in full
- `crates/callisto-model/src/` — wherever `ChangelogInput`, `ChangelogEntry`, `ChangeSource` are defined

## Bugs to fix

**Bug 5 (Medium)**: `render_section()` does `format!("- {summary}\n")` where `summary` may be a multi-line string. CommonMark requires continuation lines in a list item to be indented by at least 2 spaces. A two-paragraph summary like:

```
Fix the parser crash.

This crash was caused by a null dereference.
```

renders as:
```
- Fix the parser crash.

This crash was caused by a null dereference.
```

A markdown renderer produces: a list with one item, then a separate top-level paragraph. The fix: when inserting a multi-line summary into a list item, replace each `\n` in the summary with `\n  ` (newline + 2 spaces) so continuation lines stay within the list item per CommonMark.

**Bug 6 (Medium)**: No guard against an empty `summary` string. An empty summary emits `"- \n"` — a blank bullet. The fix: if `summary.trim().is_empty()`, skip the entry entirely (don't emit a bullet for it). Or, if every entry would be empty, return an error — but skipping is simpler and safer.

## Task

### Step 1: Write failing tests

In the `#[cfg(test)]` block of `render.rs` (or add one if absent):

**Test 5a** `render_section_indents_multiline_summary_continuation_lines`:
- Create a `ChangelogInput` with one entry whose summary is `"First line.\n\nSecond paragraph."` 
- Call `render_section()`
- Assert the result does NOT contain `"\nSecond paragraph."` (unindented)
- Assert the result DOES contain `"\n  Second paragraph."` (2-space indented) or `"\n  \n  Second paragraph."` (blank line also indented)
- Confirm the test fails before the fix

**Test 5b** `render_section_handles_trailing_newline_in_summary`:
- Summary: `"Fix bug.\n"` (trailing newline)
- Assert output doesn't contain `"- Fix bug.\n\n"` (doubled blank lines)

**Test 6** `render_section_skips_entry_with_empty_summary`:
- Create a `ChangelogInput` with two entries: one with `summary: ""` and one with `summary: "Real change"`
- Call `render_section()`
- Assert the result does NOT contain `"- \n"` (blank bullet)
- Assert the result DOES contain `"- Real change"`

Run `cargo test -p callisto-changelog` and confirm new tests fail.

input.prompt:
TDD bug fix in a Rust codebase (Callisto). Strict red-green-refactor — failing test before any production code change.

## Files to read first

- `crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` — `prepend()` and `extract_section()` in full
- Look at the existing tests in the file's `#[cfg(test)]` block

## Bugs to fix

**Bug 7 (Medium)**: `prepend()` tries to strip the `"# {display_name}\n\n"` or `"# {display_name}\n"` prefix from the existing content. If neither matches (e.g., the stored name differs by casing, has an HTML anchor like `<a name="...">`, or the package was previously known by a different name), the `else` branch fires: it prepends the new rendered entry before the entire existing content — including the existing H1 header. The output starts with `## 2.0.0` (H2) while the H1 floats below it. The fix: the `else` branch should still insert the H1 heading for the package at the top, then the new entry, then the existing content.

**Bug 8 (Low)**: `prepend()` does not guard against inserting a version section that already exists. If called twice for the same version (e.g., after an interrupted run), the changelog will have two `## 1.0.0` sections. `extract_section()` returns only the first one. The fix: before inserting, check if the rendered version heading (e.g., `"## 1.0.0"`) already appears in the existing content. If it does, skip the write (idempotent).

**Bug 9 (Low)**: When `prepend()` reads the file at line ~24 and then writes atomically at line ~71, another concurrent call for a different package sharing the same changelog path would read stale content between those two points. The fix for single-threaded callers: this is a documentation-only concern — add a doc comment to `prepend()` noting it is not safe for concurrent calls on the same path. If the codebase ever moves to parallel apply, this note serves as a guard. (No code change needed for Bug 9 unless you find concurrent callers — just add the doc comment.)

## Task

### Step 1: Write failing tests

**Test 7** `prepend_else_branch_inserts_h1_header_before_new_entry_when_display_name_mismatches`:
- Build existing content: `"# old-name\n\n## 1.0.0\n\nOld stuff\n"`
- Call `prepend("new-name", "## 2.0.0\n\n### Patch Changes\n\n- Something\n", existing)`
- Assert the result STARTS WITH `"# new-name\n\n"` (H1 at top)
- Assert `"## 2.0.0"` appears before `"## 1.0.0"` in the output
- Assert the result does NOT start with `"## 2.0.0"` (H2 at very top without H1)
- Confirm it fails before the fix

**Test 8** `prepend_is_idempotent_for_same_version`:
- Build existing content that already contains `"## 1.0.0\n\nSome content"` for a package
- Call `prepend("my-pkg", "## 1.0.0\n\nNew content\n", existing)`
- Assert the result contains `"## 1.0.0"` exactly ONCE (count occurrences — should be 1)
- Assert "Some content" is still present (idempotent = existing content preserved)
- Confirm it fails before the fix (currently it would insert a second `## 1.0.0`)

Run `cargo test -p callisto-changelog` and confirm new tests fail.

### Step 2: Fix `prepend()` in `write.rs`

**Fix for Bug 7**: In the `else` branch (when neither strip_prefix matched), instead of just doing `format!("{rendered}\n{existing}")`, do:
```rust
format!("# {display_name}\n\n{rendered}\n{existing}")
```
This ensures the H1 is always present at the top even when the existing file header doesn't match.

Note: after the CRLF fix from a previous session, `prepend()` may already normalize CRLF. Make sure the else-branch fix also handles CRLF normalization consistently with the if-branches.

**Fix for Bug 8**: Before the prefix-stripping logic (or right at the start of `prepend()`), extract just the version heading from `rendered` — the first line of `rendered`. Check if `existing` already contains that exact heading. If it does, return `existing` unchanged (idempotency — no write needed, or just return the existing content so the caller can skip the write).

**Fix for Bug 9**: Add a doc comment to `prepend()` noting: "Not safe for concurrent calls on the same `path`; callers must ensure sequential access per changelog file."

### Step 3: Run and verify

```
cargo test -p callisto-changelog
cargo clippy -p callisto-changelog -- -D warnings
```

All tests must pass, clippy must be clean.

Do not commit. Leave all changes in the working tree.

**Current state**: each package gets its own `CHANGELOG.md` at its configured path. There's no root-level aggregated view.

**What a combined changelog would look like**: a single file at the repo root (e.g. `CHANGELOG.md`) that groups all package changes per release, formatted like:

```markdown
## 2026-08-04

### @scope/pkg-a — 2.1.0
- Fix the frobnication bug

### @scope/pkg-b — 1.0.1 (cascade)
- Released together with pkg-a
```

This is a reasonable follow-on feature once the per-package changelogs are actually correct (which they're not yet, given the critical `"Release update"` bug). The config (`callisto.toml`) would need a `[changelog] combined = "CHANGELOG.md"` option to opt into it. Worth speccing before building.

content.text:
Good question — let me answer the design while the commits run.

**Opinionated defaults (no config needed):**
- Combined changelog lives at `CHANGELOG.md` in the workspace root — obvious, one canonical location
- Newest release at the top, always
- H2 for the release batch header (`## 2026-08-04` or `## 2026-08-04 — 3 packages`), H3 for each package (`### pkg-name@2.1.0`)
- Per-package changelogs still always get written — combined is additive, not a replacement
- Cascade-only bumps **omitted by default** — they're noise in a high-level view

**Configurable (small surface):**
```toml
[changelog]
combined = true                # opt-in (false by default — no surprise file for existing repos)
combined-path = "CHANGELOG.md" # override location (e.g. "docs/RELEASES.md")
combined-include-cascade = false  # show cascade-only packages (default: omit them)
```

**Not configurable (intentionally):**
- Date format (ISO 8601, period)
- Heading levels (H2 date / H3 package — locked)
- Sort order (newest first, always)
- Whether per-package changelogs still write (always yes)

The combined file reads like a project-level news feed — you see at a glance what changed across the whole repo in one place, without hunting per-crate. Cascade entries would clutter it (`pkg-b@1.0.1 — Released together with pkg-a`) when readers just want the substantive changes.

input.description: Implement combined monorepo changelog feature
input.prompt:
Implement a "combined changelog" feature for Callisto, a Rust monorepo versioning tool. TDD — failing tests before any production code. Read relevant files before writing anything.

## What to build

A combined (root-level) changelog that aggregates all package changes from a single release batch into one `CHANGELOG.md` at the workspace root. This is additive — per-package changelogs still always write. The combined changelog is opt-in via config.

## Design decisions (already made, follow exactly)

**Config** (`callisto.toml`):
```toml
[changelog]
combined = true                      # opt-in, false by default
combined-path = "CHANGELOG.md"       # optional, default "CHANGELOG.md" at workspace root
combined-include-cascade = false     # optional, default false (cascade-only bumps omitted)
```

**Output format** (opinionated, no config for these):
```markdown
## 2026-08-04

### pkg-name@2.1.0

- Fix the frobnication bug
- Add new feature

### other-pkg@1.0.1

- Released in the pkg-name@2.1.0 fixed group
```

- H2 for the release date (ISO 8601 from `chrono::Local::now()` or passed in)
- H3 for each package in format `{display_name}@{new_version}`
- Packages sorted alphabetically by display_name within a release section
- Cascade/group-only bumps omitted when `combined-include-cascade = false` (default)
- Newest release prepended at top (same pattern as per-package changelogs)

## Files to read first

1. `crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` — `prepend()` function signature and implementation
2. `crates/callisto-changelog/src/render.rs` — `render_section()` to understand ChangelogInput/ChangelogEntry types
3. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs` — `plan_version()` return type and where per-package changelog writes happen; this is where you'll also call write_combined_changelog
4. `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs` — how RawConfig is structured so you know where to add the [changelog] section
5. `crates/callisto-model/src/` — look for where ChangelogWrite or equivalent is defined (the per-package write plan)

}

Also add a resolved `ChangelogConfig` to wherever the workspace's resolved config lives (read the existing config resolution code to find the right place), with defaults: `combined = false`, `combined_path = "CHANGELOG.md"`, `combined_include_cascade = false`.

    date: &str,           // ISO 8601 date string e.g. "2026-08-04"

    permit: &callisto_model::ApplyPermit,

2. Builds the new section:
